title: Login and a protected route
summary: Issue a signed JWT on login and gate a route behind it: an expiry on the token, a 401 for everything that is not a live one, and no password hash in the answer.

checkpoints.title: A correct login gets a signed token back
checkpoints.hint: jose signs through a builder: new SignJWT(claims).setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'HS256' }).setSubject(...).setExpirationTime(...).sign(SECRET_KEY). A token with no expiry does not count.

checkpoints.title: Bad credentials get 401 and no token
checkpoints.hint: Wrong password and unknown email have to look identical from outside, or the endpoint tells an attacker which addresses are registered. A body with missing fields is a 401, not a crash.

checkpoints.title: The protected route refuses everything that is not a live token
checkpoints.hint: jwtVerify, never decodeJwt: decoding reads the claims of any token at all, including one you did not sign. Its rejection is a promise rejection, so catch it and answer 401 rather than letting it become a 500.

checkpoints.title: The protected route answers with the user behind the token
checkpoints.hint: The subject claim is a string, and findUserById takes a number. Return the profile fields one at a time; spreading the user sends the password hash with it.
